doc.title: Earl Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002

title: Hines on the road; backing Flip Phillips, Getz and singers with Vernon Alley
summary: Hines handled the road details; with Alley he backed Flip Phillips, Stan Getz, Arthur Prysock and Dorothy Dandridge.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: So I was just reading somebody’s book — his book — and it was talking about that band and what a great band it was. He said Jesus, everybody in there was full of arrangers and everybody was gung ho and everybody could play, and all he had to do — he had to learn as a matter of fact. But his mind was always open. He was always studying. If some piano player would come by and do something he’d go, “How’d you do that? What was that chord?” So he was very forward thinking and had amazing technique. I learned a lot when I went out on the road with him I learned a lot about the road because see when we went out with him he handled everything. Joe Glaser would do the booking but Hines would handle all the details. He’d see where we were going to stay, he’d see that — he’d book the hotel, the transportation, if we flew or if we took the train. Every week he’d pay us you know, took out the Social Security and all that stuff. He was interesting. Now when I worked with Vernon Alley that’s when I really got a lot of exposure. We backed Flip Phillips, Flip Phillips came in as a single and so Vernon build a band around him. Let’s see Jerome was in one band, I think Pony was in another, Pony Poindexter. Then Allen Smith was in another band. He was in both the bands that they build up when Flip came. And as a matter of fact we recorded that band. Richard Wyands on piano, Vernon on bass, I was on drums, Flip, Jerome and Alan. The first time they had a trombonist. I can’t remember his name. He was from Vallejo. The second time we just had the three horns. He could play. Flip could play. Oh yeah. He could shout or he could milk a ballad. And then of course Stan Getz came through and we backed him. And he was easy to work with. He had certain things he wanted so you tried to accommodate him. Who else? Arthur Prysock was beautiful. We backed him. Oh what a voice.
Dorothy Dandridge came in, she wasn’t very happy. She cut her engagement short.
Well you can’t please absolutely everybody.
